Collect Arithmetic combinator from the marked wooden output chest. Its one-stack limit stops production when full; empty it or attach a belt to resume.
Place another independent module after its listed research unlock. Keep its raw feeds and power supplied; no plates, circuits, gears, robots, or advanced-quality equipment are external inputs.

Follow the A–G input displays on the left: A iron ore, B copper ore, C coal, D stone, E wood, F water and G crude oil. Only required inputs are present. Port spacing varies to save space; use the labeled preview when connecting each module.

Production equipment: assembling machine 2 and steel furnaces. Research Automation 2 and Advanced material processing before building. Steel furnaces use the labeled coal supply.

Each input has an item/fluid display directly above its belt or pipe. Connect from the left; both belt lanes take the shown material. Press Alt to see the labels. Display panels need Circuit network research: leave their ghosts unbuilt until then; production works without the signs.
Feed only Crude oil, Water, Iron ore, Coal into the labeled entrances on the left. Solid inputs use separate yellow belts; fluids use the marked pipe entrances.
Collect barrel from the marked wooden output chest. Its one-stack limit stops production when full; empty it or attach a belt to resume.
Place another independent module after its listed research unlock. Keep its raw feeds and power supplied; no plates, circuits, gears, robots, or advanced-quality equipment are external inputs.

Follow the A–G input displays on the left: A iron ore, B copper ore, C coal, D stone, E wood, F water and G crude oil. Only required inputs are present. Port spacing varies to save space; use the labeled preview when connecting each module.
This oil-stage module takes raw crude oil and includes basic refining.
changes: Original layout generated from the installed vanilla recipes and research tree.
All intermediates are manufactured inside. One dedicated output keeps each module independent.

blueprints.name: Yellow transport workshop · from raw materials
blueprints.author: Factorio Command Center
setupNotes: Connect external electricity to the big electric pole marked P. Medium electric poles power the machines and inserters.

Research Logistics, Circuit network, Fast inserter, Automation 2, Advanced material processing, Electric Energy Distribution 1. Circuit network is required for production: keep the green wires, belt reader and item limits intact.
Feed only Iron ore, Copper ore, Coal at the labeled left-side ports. All smelting and intermediate products are made inside. No robots required.

Each input has an item/fluid display directly above its belt or pipe. Connect from the left; both belt lanes take the shown material. Press Alt to see the labels. Display panels need Circuit network research: leave their ghosts unbuilt until then; production works without the signs.
Uses assembling machine 2, steel furnaces, yellow circulating belts and filtered fast inserters.
The circulating belt shares ingredients between machines. 4 iron furnaces supply the chain. The controls limit circulating stock and reserve ingredients for other recipes.
Collect the three transport products from their separate numbered wooden chests. Each chest holds one stack. Empty it or connect an output belt to continue making that item.
Yellow belts also feed underground belts and splitters internally. The belt output chest fills once the circulating supply has a reserve.
changes: Shared smelting and a controlled circulating belt feed all three transport outputs.

notes: Inputs are recipe ingredients and recognized machine fuels or fluids supplied from outside. Outputs are products not consumed by another included process. Check belt, pipe, and robot connections in-game; this analysis does not simulate routing or throughput.

Supply every labeled operating input, including fluids where listed, and external electricity. Preserve stock controls, circuit wires and passive-provider chest limits. Intermediates are manufactured inside; construction materials are not operating inputs.
Needs supplied electronic circuits: 84 per minute at the targets; 1 green-circuit supplier copy (360 per minute each) covers it.

Factorio 2.1.24 Space Age. 19 assembling machine 2 (no modules), red belts, fast/long-handed/bulk arms. WEST inputs, one labelled entrance each: iron plates, electronic circuits, copper plates, steel plates, stone bricks, plastic bars. EAST: eight passive provider chests in one column, one product each; each stops at its own cap, set in the constant combinator beside the fast-belt chest (edit one number). Gears, cable, red circuits, yellow belts, undergrounds, splitters, inserters and AM1 are made inside. Preserve the red ring wires, the green cap wires, all arm filters, the entrance belt conditions, the gear clock, the fast-inserter reserve decider and the fast-inserter feed decider. Supply electricity at the marked substation.

Feed each west entrance with its labelled material only; the harness feeds every entrance as a full red belt. Iron mostly goes to the rear belt behind the bottom row, which feeds three iron-gear-wheel machines and the underground-belt, assembling-machine-1 and transport-belt machines. The electric-mining-drill, splitter, inserter and fast-inserter machines take iron from the ring, which gets it through one admission arm fed by a bulk arm that lifts iron off the rear belt.
Electronic circuits are a supplied input (84/min at the floors, more when one product is drawn alone); one green-circuits supplier covers this mall.
Caps live in one constant combinator next to the fast-belt chest (one negative number per product). Each chest arm runs only while its product is below its cap.

Fast inserters are also a bulk-inserter ingredient. The fast-inserter machine's inserter-feed arm runs while the fast-inserter chest is below its cap or the ring holds fewer than 4 fast inserters (one decider), so the bulk-inserter machine keeps getting fast inserters while that chest is full. A second decider lets the fast-inserter chest arm take only fast inserters above a ring reserve of 14.
Gear arms of the six gear-hungry finals take turns in an eight-window clock (7.5 s each); yellow belts, inserters and AM1 take gears freely because their own ring limits bound them.

Plan supply above the entrance panels if all eight products should hold their floors at once: the panels are recipe totals at the floors, and products early on the ring run above them and take material first. Exploration measurements (full-length runs with a throttled-feed copy of the harness, not part of the qualification): with every entrance fed at exactly its panel figure and all eight products drawn, assembling machine 2 made 0/min (floor 2) and bulk inserters 0.25/min (floor 1); the other six held their floors. The floors need about the measured draw: 195 electronic circuits, 722 iron, 38 steel, 27 stone brick, 30 plastic and 30 copper per minute, two to three times the panels. Circuits alone limited to 360/min (one green-circuits copy) with every other entrance unlimited kept all eight above their floors. With less supply the mall still fills every chest in turn; only the all-eight-at-once floors are lost.
Game profile: Factorio 2.1.24.

Robot network: leave the starter pack and the platform parts in the kit's passive provider chests, inside one roboport network with logistic robots that also covers the rocket silo. With "Automatic requests from space platforms" on, the silo takes its cargo from that network and refuses cargo put in by hand. The kit makes no roboports or robots.

First launch: in a save that has never created a space platform, the asteroid collector and crusher recipes unlock only when the first platform is created, so the kit fills 14 of its 16 chests and waits (blueprint-sources/launch-kit/history/first-launch-order). Place the silo and create the platform as soon as the silo and the starter pack are ready; the kit then makes the crusher and the four collectors by itself and the last cargo rocket waits for them. The measured kit time applies to a save where a platform already exists.
Needs supplied concrete: 23 per minute at the panel figure; 1 concrete supplier copy covers it.

Needs supplied electronic circuit: 127 per minute at the panel figure; 1 green-circuit supplier copy covers it. One green-circuits copy (360/min) covers the kit and rocket supplies together; split its exit belt between them.

serviceInputs: Power for machines and inserters
notes: Inputs are recipe ingredients and recognized machine fuels or fluids supplied from outside. Outputs are products not consumed by another included process. Check belt, pipe, and robot connections in-game; this analysis does not simulate routing or throughput.

Supply every labeled operating input, including fluids where listed, at or above its panel figure, and external electricity. Preserve stock controls, circuit wires and passive-provider chest limits. Construction materials are not operating inputs.
Rocket fuel passes straight through to its own chest; it is supplied, not made here.
Needs supplied rocket fuel: 5 per minute at the panel figure; 1 rocket-fuel supplier copy covers it.

Needs supplied electronic circuit: 120 per minute at the panel figure; 1 green-circuit supplier copy covers it. No clear row north of the circuit entrance (the copper, plastic and steel entrances sit on the rows just above it, all four side-loading onto the ring's west column), so a green-circuits copy cannot sit directly west with its exit on this row without covering the copper, plastic, steel and acid approaches: place it further south or west and bring its belt in on row 10.

Factorio 2.1.24 Space Age, normal quality: assembling machine 2 only, no modules, red belts, fast inserters. Makes processing units and low density structures at 5 per minute each and passes rocket fuel through, so the three rocket ingredients (50 of each per rocket) wait side by side in three passive provider chests on the EAST edge: rocket fuel, processing units, low density structures from the north, 400 each (chest bars). WEST entrances: rocket fuel (northernmost, from one rocket-fuel supplier), copper plate, plastic bar, steel plate, electronic circuits (southernmost, from a green-circuit supplier) on belts and sulfuric acid by pipe; each panel gives the supply to plan for. Supply electricity at the substation. Preserve the red wires on the ring tiles, entrance belts and arms (per-tile hold readers and stock limits), the arm filters and the chest bars.

Supply per minute (the entrance panels): rocket-fuel 5, copper-plate 120, plastic-bar 45, steel-plate 10, electronic-circuit 120, sulfuric-acid 25. One rocket-fuel supplier (6 per minute) covers the rocket fuel; one green-circuit supplier (360 per minute) covers these 120 circuits and the launch kit's together, split its exit belt between them.

Paste it anywhere on a platform made from one starter pack: it snaps to the hub.
